details: Senate Republicans have released a revised version of the CLARITY Act, a significant piece of legislation aimed at establishing a clearer regulatory framework for digital assets in the United States. Key revisions include enforceable ethics proposals for federal officials with substantial crypto interests, requiring them to divest or place assets in blind trusts. The bill also modifies stablecoin regulations, introducing a "circuit breaker" that allows the Treasury Secretary to intervene if stablecoins cause significant withdrawals from community banks. A crucial cloture vote is scheduled for September 15th, with Polymarket traders currently estimating a 32% probability of the bill's passage in 2026. The anti-CBDC section, previously a standalone component, has been removed, though restrictions on central bank digital currencies remain in the introductory language of the bill.
title: US Senate Advances Revised CLARITY Act for Crypto Regulation

details: The Federal Reserve is facing intense scrutiny as it approaches its September 15-16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, where markets are pricing in a high probability (around 90%) of another interest rate hike. This comes despite a cooling labor market, with the decision complicated by the impending September 30th release of the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, which will include a sweeping annual revision of historical inflation data dating back to 2021. Analysts suggest these revisions could significantly alter the perceived inflation landscape, potentially impacting the Fed's future monetary policy trajectory. This period of uncertainty, coupled with rising US Treasury yields and hawkish macroeconomic repricing, has already contributed to selling pressure on Bitcoin and led to net capital outflows from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recently.
title: Fed Rate Hike Debates Intensify Amid Upcoming PCE Data Revisions
